name: minimal
source: Shared with the encoder contract in contracts/plan/testdata, where the file is the canonical output and the JSON is the input. Contract rules: Document, Version.

name: strings
source: Shared with the encoder contract in contracts/plan/testdata, where the file is the canonical output and the JSON is the input. Contract rule: Strings. Each quoted value is text, and each plain value is one clause of the plain rule.

name: multiline
source: Shared with the encoder contract in contracts/plan/testdata, where the file is the canonical output and the JSON is the input. Contract rule: Strings, block and quoted forms.

name: answers
source: Shared with the encoder contract in contracts/plan/testdata, where the file is the canonical output and the JSON is the input. Contract rule: Values. The plain word deferred is the Deferred value, the quoted one is text.

name: unknown-fields
source: Shared with the encoder contract in contracts/plan/testdata, where the file is the canonical output and the JSON is the input. Contract rule: Unknown fields. 0030: unknown fields are preserved.

name: key-order
source: Shared with the encoder contract in contracts/plan/testdata, where the file is the canonical output and the JSON is the input. Contract rule: every known key is read.

name: conditions
source: Shared with the encoder contract in contracts/plan/testdata, where the file is the canonical output and the JSON is the input. Condition syntax is from docs/reference/section-template-schema/conditions.md.

name: list-order
source: Hand-written. Every array field holds several items out of sorted order, with a repeat in some, so a version that sorts, reverses, or drops repeats fails. Contract rule: Lists, and the order of items in a plan.

name: acme
source: The ACME example plan. The JSON is shared with the encoder contract, which was converted from this file and then checked and fixed by hand.

name: hand-edited
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Style is free. A person edits a plan by hand, so comments, a document marker, flow style, single quotes, folded and keep blocks, any key order, any indent, a plain date in a string field and in an unknown field, and the plain keys on, 1, and y are read as they were meant. 0030: plans decode leniently. The quoted key "<<" is an ordinary key. The largest and smallest 64-bit integers are read as int64 in an unknown field. A quoted true, number, null, or empty string in an unknown field is text.

name: no-final-newline
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Style is free. A file need not end in a newline.

name: control-characters
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Reading the file. The decoder does not judge the characters of a quoted string, so an escaped NUL and bell are kept.

name: zero-and-null
source: Hand-written. Contract rules: Null and empty values, Strings. 0030: null is null or an omitted key. deferred is the Deferred value only where an answer or a default is read.

name: value-lists-in-conditions
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Values. A list in isOneOf is a List Value, and an empty one is a List with no items.

name: null-env-values
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Known fields. A null value in a step's env is the empty string.

name: null-maps
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Known fields. A null or absent map is nil. A scope under answers.sections that is null or empty is a kept, empty map.

name: answers-plan-only
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Known fields. A map that is present is not nil, even when empty.

name: answers-null
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Known fields. A null answers is the zero Answers.

name: answers-sections-null
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Known fields. A null answers.sections is nil.

name: quoted-keys
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Style is free. A quoted key is the same key as a plain one, including schemaVersion.

name: unvalidated
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Not covered. Validating is the plan validator's job, per the components doc, so values pass through unchanged.

name: not-yaml
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, file.not-yaml.

name: tab-indent
source: Hand-written. YAML forbids a tab for indentation.

name: invalid-utf8
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Document. The bytes must be UTF-8.

name: utf16
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, file.not-yaml. UTF-16 is not UTF-8, even with a byte order mark.

name: empty-file
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, file.not-a-plan.

name: lone-marker
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, file.not-a-plan.

name: empty-map
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Version. A top-level map without schemaVersion.

name: comments-only
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, file.not-a-plan.

name: root-list
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, file.not-a-plan.

name: root-scalar
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, file.not-a-plan.

name: multiple-documents
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, file.multiple-documents.

name: multiple-documents-empty
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, file.multiple-documents. A second document counts even when it is empty.

name: empty-documents
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems. A document with nothing in it is empty, and an empty first document comes before a second one.

name: null-document-then-second
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems. A document that holds null is not empty, so the second document is reported.

name: tagged-null-document-then-second
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems. A tag is ignored, so a first document with only an empty tagged scalar is empty.

name: anchored-empty-document-then-second
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems. An anchor is a node, so a first document with an anchored empty scalar is not empty.

name: quoted-empty-document-then-second
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems. A quoted empty string is text, so a first document holding it is not empty.

name: syntax-error-after-empty-document
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems. A syntax error anywhere in the file comes before every other file problem.

name: non-map-with-second-document
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems. File problems are checked in a fixed order, and a second document comes before the type of the top level.

name: parse-error-in-second-document
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems. A syntax error anywhere in the file comes before a second document.

name: version-missing
source: Hand-written. 0030, Versioning: schemaVersion is an integer. Contract rule: Version.

name: version-quoted
source: Hand-written. 0030, Versioning: schemaVersion is an integer, so the text 1 is not one.

name: version-decimal
source: Hand-written. 0030, Versioning: schemaVersion is an integer.

name: version-boolean
source: Hand-written. A version problem is the only problem reported, so the spelling yes is not reported as well.

name: version-leading-zero
source: Hand-written. 0030 format guards: a leading zero is not read as a number.

name: version-hex
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Version. Any number spelling that is not a canonical integer is invalid, and a version problem is the only problem.

name: version-out-of-range
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Version. An integer that does not fit in 64 bits is not a version.

name: version-list
source: Hand-written. 0030, Versioning: schemaVersion is an integer.

name: version-zero
source: Hand-written. 0030, Versioning: older than supported is refused, with the versions supported.

name: version-negative
source: Hand-written. 0030, Versioning: older than supported is refused.

name: version-negative-zero
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Version. -0 is a canonical integer below 1, and found is the text as written.

name: version-plus-zero
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Version. A plus sign makes a number spelling.

name: version-underscore
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Version. An underscore makes a number spelling.

name: version-too-new
source: Hand-written. 0030, Versioning: newer than the tool knows is refused with a message to upgrade. The file also holds the spelling yes, which is not reported.

name: version-too-new-with-other-problems
source: Hand-written. A file of a newer version may use anything, so only the version problem is reported, even for an anchor and an alias, and when schemaVersion is the last key.

name: duplicate-version
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Version. With two schemaVersion keys the version is not known, so neither wins.

name: duplicate-version-bad-values
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Version. Two schemaVersion keys are the only problem, whatever their values.

name: alias-on-version
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Version. An anchor on schemaVersion is an alias problem, and the version is still read.

name: anchor-on-root
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, format.alias. An anchor on the top-level map is an alias problem with no path.

name: complex-key
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Reading the file, Keys. A key that is not a scalar is a wrong type, at the path of the map that holds it.

name: complex-key-in-section
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Keys, as in complex-key, inside a section.

name: complex-key-then-problem
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Keys. Every key that is not a scalar is reported, and the entries after it are still read.

name: alias-key
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Keys. An alias used as a key is a key that is not a scalar, and its place is the map that holds it, so it comes before the anchor on the later line.

name: version-too-new-with-anchor
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Version. An anchor on a bad version is only the version problem.

name: version-key-as-value
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Version. Only a key is read as schemaVersion, and a value of that text is not.

name: version-nine
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Version. Every digit is read in decimal.

name: version-largest
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Version. The largest 64-bit integer fits, so it is too new and not invalid.

name: version-alias
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Version. An alias in place of the value is version.invalid, and the anchor elsewhere is not reported.

name: boolean-spelling
source: Hand-written. 0030 format guards: an unquoted yes, no, on, off, y, n, True, or TRUE is an error. Every spelling is listed on purpose, in each case form, and in a text, a boolean, a list, a map, and an unknown field. A spelling where a list belongs is the spelling problem alone.

name: number-spelling
source: Hand-written. 0030 format guards: numbers that parse surprisingly, such as 1.0 or a leading zero, are errors where a string is meant. Contract rule: Numbers. The ok values are text that only looks like a number, and the x-ok map holds the numbers that are allowed in an unknown field. A sign may precede any non-canonical form, the prefixes and the exponent letter may be upper case, and a decimal too large for a float64 is a problem.

name: number-edges
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Numbers. The a values are number spellings, with underscores between digits in any part, and the ok values are text that only looks like a number.

name: null-spelling
source: Hand-written. 0030 format guards: null is null or an omitted key. Contract rule: Null and empty values. Only those three spellings are null, so nULL and NuLL are text.

name: tags
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Reading the file, Tags. A tag is ignored, so the scalar is read by its text and style.

name: empty-answer
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, format.empty-answer. It mirrors the encoder's encode.empty-answer. A null or an omitted key is allowed for default and is.

name: alias
source: Hand-written. 0030 format guards: anchors and aliases are rejected. The merge key is reported once, at the key, whatever its value is. An anchor inside an unknown field counts too. An alias in place of a map is the alias problem. An anchor on a key is reported at the key's path. The entries after a merge key are still read. The value of a merge key is not read, so the yes in it is not reported.

name: merge-keys
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, format.alias. Each merge key is one alias problem, and a repeated merge key is not also a duplicate key.

name: anchored-null
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems. An anchor is reported wherever it is written, and the other problem of the node follows it.

name: duplicate-key
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, format.duplicate-key. Each key after the first is reported. The quoted key counts as the same key. The value of the second key is read, and a map in an unknown field is checked.

name: wrong-type
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, format.wrong-type. The domain model gives the type of each field. A map or list inside a value of the wrong type is not read, so the yes in them is not reported. A canonical number where a list belongs is a wrong type.

name: wrong-type-answers
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Values. The domain model says a Value is text, a flag, a list of text, or deferred. A plain true or false is not text, so it is a wrong type as an item of a List Value too.

name: wrong-type-answers-shape
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, format.wrong-type. The domain model gives Answers two maps.

name: wrong-type-items
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, format.wrong-type. A plain text where a condition clause, an answer test, or a step belongs is a wrong type, and the decoder goes on without it.

name: wrong-type-same-place
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems. A map and its first key start at the same place, and two problems with the same code there come parent first.

name: unknown-field
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Unknown fields. The domain model keeps unknown fields on a plan and on a section only. The x-allowed key on the section is kept.

name: unknown-field-values
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Unknown fields. The value of an unknown key is not read, every unknown key is reported, including a repeated one, and an anchor on the key is still an alias problem.

name: many-problems
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems. All problems are reported, in the order of the file.

name: same-place
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems. Two problems at one place come in the order of the table: the spelling, then the anchor.

name: empty-item
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, format.empty-item. It mirrors the encoder's encode.empty-item, because dropping a null item would shift the list. A List Value is a list, so a null item in one counts.

name: switch
source: Shared with the encoder contract in contracts/plan/testdata, where the file is the canonical output and the JSON is the input. ACME-style sections. Contract rules: Known fields and Section clauses. 0050: a switched-off section, an explicit true that is kept, an absent switch that stays absent, and a section clause in includeIf and askIf.

name: enabled-values
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Section clauses, Known fields. 0050: enabled true and false on a section, absent or null is none, a variable and answers named enabled are ordinary, a quoted section id is text, and x-enabled is an unknown field.

name: enabled-wrong-type
source: Hand-written. Contract rules: Problems, Section clauses. A boolean field takes a plain true or false, so a quoted false, the number 0 or 1.5, a list, or a map is format.wrong-type, in a section and in a section clause. A section id that is a list or a plain true is a wrong type too.

name: enabled-spelling
source: Hand-written. 0030 format guards. A plain yes, Off, no, TRUE, or n where enabled belongs is format.boolean-spelling, in a section and in a section clause, and not a wrong type.

name: clause-forms
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Section clauses. A clause with a section key is a section clause whatever the order of its keys, and its question and answer are keys it does not know. Without a section key, enabled is a key a question clause does not know. The value of an unknown key is not read, so the plain yes is not reported.

name: clause-missing-enabled
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Section clauses. The model cannot tell an absent enabled from false, so a section clause with no enabled, an empty one, or a null one is refused and not read as false. A ~ is the null spelling alone. At one place the table order puts format.wrong-type before format.unknown-field.

name: clause-empty-section
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Section clauses. The decoder does not validate, so an empty, null, or blank section id is read as the empty string and the plan validator judges it. A section key that is present makes it a section clause.

name: example-values
source: Hand-written. Contract rules: Known fields, Scalars, Values. A variable's example is a string field like its description, so a quoted or plain string is text, absent, empty, and null are the empty string, and a plain deferred is text because a string is not a Value. 0030 and the example brief: example sits beside description in a variable at the plan and in a section.

name: example-problems
source: Hand-written. Contract rules: Problems, Scalars, Numbers, Known fields. example is a string field like description, so a list, a map, and a plain true or false are wrong-type, a plain canonical number or hex is number-spelling, a plain yes is a boolean spelling, a plain ~ is the null spelling, an anchor is reported before the wrong type of the same node, a repeated key is reported once, and a key with other case or spelling is an unknown field. A wrong-type value is not read, so the yes in the map is not reported.

name: parent-values
source: Hand-written. 0070 and the sub-sections brief: parent is a plain text field read like title, so a quoted or plain string is text, absent, empty, and null are the empty string and the same as a root, a plain deferred is text, and a plain date is text. A parent that names no section, the section itself, or a cycle is kept as written, because the plan validator checks the structure. Contract rule: Known fields. Parent, x-parent, and parents are unknown fields, and a section or a variable named parent is ordinary.

name: parent-problems
source: Hand-written. Contract rules: Problems, Scalars, Numbers, Known fields. parent is a string field like title and example, so a plain yes or Off is a boolean spelling, a plain ~ or NULL is the null spelling, a plain canonical or hex number is number-spelling, a plain true or false, a list, and a map are wrong-type, an anchor is reported before the wrong type of the same node, a repeated key is reported once, and a quoted yes is text. A wrong-type value is not read, so the yes in the map is not reported.

name: origin-values
source: Hand-written. ADR 0075 (Identity and origin) and the domain model (Plan, Origin): a plan has an optional text `id`, and a personal plan an optional `origin` with `planId`, `source`, `contentHash`, and `refreshedOn`, all text, the date in ISO form like `generatedOn`. Contract rule: Known fields. Key order is free, a plain UUID, a plain date, and a URL are text, and `Origin`, `ID`, and `x-id` on the plan, `origin` and `x-origin` on a section, and a variable, an answer, or a section named `id` or `origin` are ordinary.

name: origin-partial
source: Hand-written. Domain model, Origin: every field is optional, so an origin with only a `source` keeps that one and leaves the plan `id` empty. Contract rule: Known fields.

name: origin-empty
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Known fields, a key whose value is null, empty, or absent is the zero value. Domain model: `id` and `origin` are optional, so an empty `id` and a null `origin` are the same as absent.

name: origin-blank
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Known fields. An `origin` whose four keys are empty, null, or quoted empty is the same as no `origin`, because the model holds an Origin value and cannot tell them apart. An empty `id` is the empty string.

name: origin-empty-map
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Known fields. `origin: {}` is an empty Origin, the same as absent.

name: origin-strings
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Known fields and Scalars. A string field is text, so quoted `yes`, `null`, and `0123` stay text, with their spaces and capitals as written, and a plain `deferred` is text in `source` because a string is not a Value. ADR 0075: the ids are text.

name: origin-problems
source: Hand-written. Contract rules: Problems, Scalars, and Unknown fields. `origin` is a map that cannot keep unknown fields, like `provenance`, so `extra` and `PlanId` are `format.unknown-field` at the key. A plain `123` is a number spelling and a plain `yes` a boolean spelling in a text field, and a plain `true` or a list is `format.wrong-type`. An anchor on the `id` is `format.alias`, and a repeated `planId` is a duplicate key.

name: origin-anchor
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, format.alias. An anchor on the `origin` map is reported at its path, and the map is still read.

name: origin-wrong-type
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, format.wrong-type. A map where `id` belongs and a list where `origin` belongs are not read, so the plain `yes` inside the map is not reported.

name: origin-scalar
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, format.wrong-type. A list in `id` and a plain text in `origin`, which holds a mapping.

name: id-spelling
source: Hand-written. Contract rules: Scalars and Numbers. A plain `yes`, `~`, and `0x1F` where text belongs are spelling problems, at `id` and at the keys of `origin`.

name: origin-duplicate
source: Hand-written. Contract rules: Problems, format.duplicate-key. The path of a duplicate key is the second and later keys, and the value of a duplicate key is read like any other, so the unknown key in the second `origin` is reported.

name: directory-shared
source: Hand-written YAML for the shared plan in contracts/plan/testdata/directory.plan.json. ADR 0080 (Directory) and the domain model (Directory, Contact, Role, Team): the 0080 example, with a quoted `@sam` and `#it-help`, a plain `U01ABC123`, a contact with only an id and a name, a role with no holders, and a team with no holders. Contract rule: Directory.

name: directory-team-contact
source: Hand-written. ADR 0080: a team may name a `contact`, the id of a directory contact, and the contact never stands in for a role holder. Contract rule: Directory, a team's `contact`. It is text read like `title`, in any key order, kept as written: quoted `"42"`, `'true'`, `"yes"`, `'null'`, and `"\u0040oncall"` are text, a plain `deferred`, a plain date, and a literal block are text, spaces and case are kept. An absent, null, empty, or bare `contact` is the empty string. An id that names no contact passes through, and a contact never appears in a team's `holders`, with or without them, so a team with only a contact, with an empty `holders` map, or with a vacant entry is read as written.

name: directory-team-contact-problems
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, and Directory. A team's `contact` is a string read like a `title`: a list, a map, and a plain `true` are `format.wrong-type` at `directory.teams[n].contact`, a plain `yes`, `Off`, `no`, `42`, `0x1F`, and `1e3` are spelling problems, an anchor is `format.alias`, and a repeated key is `format.duplicate-key`. Problems come in file order: team 10 has `holders` before `contact`, and team 11 has `contact` before `holders` and `name`.

name: directory-team-contact-elsewhere
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Directory. `contact` is a key of a team only. In a contact or a role it is an unknown field, and the anchor and the `0x1F` in those values are not read. On a team the key is exact: `Contact`, `contacts`, `team-contact`, `x-contact`, and `contactId` are unknown, and the exact `contact: sam` beside them is no problem.

name: directory-values
source: Hand-written. ADR 0080 (Directory) and the domain model (Directory, Contact, Role, Team). Contract rule: Directory. The directory comes after the sections, its three lists are in reverse order, every item lists its keys backwards, flow style and block style are mixed, and a team's `holders` keys are not in sorted order, so a version that depends on file order or on key order fails. A contact, a role, and a team may hold only an id. Nothing is filled in.

name: directory-strings
source: Hand-written. Contract rules: Scalars, Directory. Every directory field and every holder is a string read like a `title`: quoted `"42"`, `'true'`, `"yes"`, and `'null'` are text, a plain `deferred` is text, a plain date is text, `~sam@host` is text, `"\u0040sam"` is `@sam`, spaces are kept, and a literal block is text with a newline. A team's `holders` keys `on`, `y`, `1`, `yes`, and `null` are the text as written. `"yes": []` is a vacant role.

name: directory-blank
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Directory. A `directory` with nothing after it is null, and the plan holds the zero Directory, like an empty `origin`.

name: directory-empty-map
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Directory. `directory: {}` is the zero Directory, the same plan as a null `directory`.

name: directory-empty-lists
source: Hand-written. ADR 0080 (Directory) and the domain model (Directory, Contact, Role, Team) and the resolution order in 0080: a team entry for a role, even an empty one, means the role is vacant for that team. Contract rule: Directory. A null or empty list is nil. A team's absent or null `holders` is nil, and `holders: {}` is an empty map that is not nil. A role entry that is `[]` or null stays in the map with no items, so the role stays vacant for that team.

name: directory-list-order
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Directory, lists. 0080: holders are in order, and the first holder comes first. Every directory list and every list of holders is out of sorted order, and several hold repeats. Two contacts, two roles, and two teams share an id and are all kept.

name: directory-unvalidated
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Directory, the decoder does not validate. The plan validator judges these: an id that is not a lowercase slug, an id with a space, an empty id, an email with no `@`, a holder that names no contact, and a team entry for a role that does not exist. 0080 Integrity lists them.

name: directory-and-step
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Directory. A step's `directory` is its working directory and stays a string, and a section's `directory` and `x-directory` are ordinary unknown fields. Only a top-level `directory` is the plan's directory.

name: directory-unknown-field
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, and Directory. The directory, a contact, a role, and a team cannot keep unknown fields, like `provenance` and `origin`. Keys are exact: `Email`, `slack_id`, `slackid`, `Contacts`, and `x-note` are unknown, and so is a key that belongs to another kind of item, such as `holders` in a contact or `email` in a role. The value of an unknown key is not read, so the `yes`, the anchor, and the `0x1F` in `extra` are not reported.

name: directory-scalar
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, and Directory. A `directory` that is not a map is a wrong type at `directory`.

name: directory-list
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, and Directory. A `directory` that is a list is a wrong type, and nothing inside it is read, so the `yes` and the `0x1F` are not reported.

name: directory-wrong-type-lists
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, and Directory. `contacts`, `roles`, and `teams` each take a list. A text, a map, and a canonical number are wrong types at the key.

name: directory-wrong-type-items
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, and Directory. An item of `contacts`, `roles`, or `teams` that is a text, a number, a flag, or a list is a wrong type at the item, and the decoder goes on to the item that is a map.

name: directory-null-items
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, and Directory. A null item of a directory list, of a role's `holders`, or of a team's list of holders is `format.empty-item`, because dropping it would shift the list. The path of a team's holder is `directory.teams[1].holders.r[1]`.

name: directory-field-problems
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, and Directory. Every directory field is a string read like a `title`, and every holder is a string. A list, a map, and a plain `true` or `false` are wrong types, a plain `yes`, `Off`, `~`, `0x1F`, `1e3`, `007`, and a canonical `42` or `123` are spelling problems, and an anchor is `format.alias`. A role's `holders` that is a text, and a team's `holders` that is a list, are wrong types at `holders`. A team's role entry that is a text or a map is a wrong type at `holders.<role id>`, and an item inside a role entry is read at `holders.<role id>[n]`.

name: directory-anchors
source: Hand-written. 0030 format guards, and the Problems rules for anchors, aliases, and merge keys. The guards apply inside the directory: an anchor on the directory, on a list, on an item, and on a value, an alias as an item and as a value, a merge key in an item and in a team's `holders`, and an anchor on a key, which is reported at the key's path.

name: directory-duplicate-keys
source: Hand-written. 0030 format guards. A repeated key is reported at the second and later keys inside the directory: a contact field, a `contacts` key, a role id in a team's `holders`, and the `directory` key itself. A quoted key and a plain key with the same text are the same key.

name: directory-complex-key
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Style is free, a key that is not a scalar is `format.wrong-type` at the map that holds it, and the entries after it are still read. A role id in a team's `holders` and a contact field are no exception.

name: directory-problem-order
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems come in the order of their places in the file. The directory sits between `origin` and `variables`, and its problems come between theirs, so a version that reads the directory in a second pass fails.

name: directory-version-too-new
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Version. A newer file may use anything, so a `directory` that is a list with a plain `yes` in it is not read, and the version problem is the only problem.
